root_idea.summary: The root primarily conveys rising, height, and loftiness.
root_idea.development: The physical image of upward growth, especially in tall palms, extends to elevated clouds, superiority in reputation, and mastery in knowledge. The saliva-related branch is treated in the lexical evidence as an interchange with بَصَقَ rather than as part of the elevation branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is normalized to the singular active-participle citation form بَاسِقٌ.

senses.definition: Tall, lofty, or fully grown in stature.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the plural بَاسِقَاتٍ describes palms as tall and upward-growing in Q 50:10; the related nuance of full growth is treated as part of this height sense, not as a separate meaning.
An alternative interpretation of بَاسِقَاتٍ in Q 50:10, associated with the Form IV usage describing a female animal as pregnant or bearing before parturition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass others in excellence, fame, or renown; to rise above them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use, including constructions with عَلَيْهِمْ or بِهِمْ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become skilled in a science, mastering its abstrusities and niceties or the whole of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي in the expression بَسَقَ فِي عِلْمِهِ.
A rare or disputed use; some authorities restrict بَسَقَ to the meaning of excessive tallness, while others equate this use with بَصَقَ or بَزَقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sun rose or appeared above the horizon.
To be prolix or tedious; in one usage, to be heavy or sluggish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form II/Form V usage, especially in the expression لَا تُبَسِّقْ عَلَيْنَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To secrete first milk or colostrum into the udder before giving birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a ewe or she-camel, typically about a month or more before parturition and sometimes even when not pregnant; it can also describe a virgin girl whose breasts develop milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stony tract, such as a ḥarrah, or somewhat elevated ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is given as بِسَاقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Spittle or saliva after it has left the mouth, especially saliva that flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use equated with بُصَاقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clear white stone that glistens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal expression, also recorded with the ṣād spelling.
Applied to a ewe or she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds: high and clear-white; بَوَاسِقُ can also denote their first appearing portions or elongated upper summits, and by extension chamomile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use applied to clouds and, through the shape of their elevated or elongated heads, to the named plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Endowed with elevated or noble natural dispositions and mental qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction describing elevated character or mental qualities.
A rare nominal use; the transmitted identification is accompanied by a textual uncertainty in the lexical source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female camel that secretes first milk or colostrum before giving birth; also a virgin girl whose breasts have flowing milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participle use corresponding to the early-milk sense of أَبْسَقَ.

cautions: The fruit-bearing interpretation of Q 50:10 is an alternative lexical interpretation; the supplied Quran contextual gloss supports the tall interpretation.
The saliva meaning of بَسَقَ is reported as rare or disputed and is associated in the root discussion with the separate بَصَقَ branch.
